extracted.intended_audience: news organizations and their communications/publicity staff (radio, television, digital outlets) who win or promote Edward R. Murrow Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Official promotion and brand-usage guidelines for organizations that have won Regional or National Edward R. Murrow Awards, including required wording, logo/medallion usage, social media recommendations, and trophy/plaque rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional award naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Use “Regional Murrow Award” or “Regional Edward R. Murrow Award”. Do not use “Murrow Award” without including Regional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise in wording when referring to regional wins; explicitly include the word "Regional."

rubrics_metrics.name: National award naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Use “Murrow Award,” “Edward R. Murrow Award” or “National Murrow Award” when referring to national-level awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve the unqualified term "Murrow Award" (and the medallion) for national winners per the page's distinction between regional and national usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement language — do not use 'nominated'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use “under consideration for a National Murrow Award” or “advancing to the National Murrow Award competition”. Do not use “nominated”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use one of the approved phrases to describe a regional winner's status in the national competition; avoid claiming a "nomination."

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization name usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use RTDNA or Radio Television Digital News Association. DO NOT use RTNDA or Radio Television News Directors Association (these are former names).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always use the current organization name(s) as provided; explicitly avoid former acronyms/names that are no longer correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo usage — regional winners
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional winners may use either the square logo or rectangular banner, including the "winner" banner. Regional winners may not use the medallion or Murrow silhouette image alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided regional logo assets (square or rectangular/winner banner). Do not isolate or use the medallion/silhouette if you are a regional winner; download logos from the RTDNA site as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo/medallion usage — national winners
rubrics_metrics.description: National Murrow Award winners may use the Murrow Award logos as well as the Murrow medallion, which can be downloaded (Murrow Medallion JPG, PNG, EPS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The medallion and logos are explicitly allowed for national winners; assets are provided for download in multiple formats for use in promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add award to professional bios
rubrics_metrics.description: Add “Edward R. Murrow Award Winner” to your professional biography and social media profile bios, including LinkedIn, Facebook and Twitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations and individuals associated with a winning entry may update bios to include the specified award wording; follow the naming rules (regional vs national) when applying this guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share winning piece with explanatory commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Share a link to the Murrow-winning piece across your social media platforms and add commentary that explains how it demonstrates responsible journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sharing, remember to tag @RTDNA and use #Murrow. Include context about why the piece matters and how it aligns with RTDNA values/ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested messaging about award significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain to your audience why winning a Murrow Award matters using the provided language: the Murrow Awards are the embodiment of the values, principles and standards set forth by Edward R. Murrow... Murrow Award winning stories put public interest above all else, provide a catalyst for public discussion, and adhere to the RTDNA Code of Ethics. Of the awards given to journalists, the Murrow Awards are among the most respected journalism awards in the world. Responsible journalism helps to expose corruption and shines a light on problems that would otherwise go unnoticed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these approved phrases in press releases, social posts, and biographies to describe the award's prestige and alignment with journalistic ethics. The page also suggests sharing Edward Murrow quotes to reinforce the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Edward R. Murrow quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Share some of Edward Murrow’s most famous quotes about the value of journalism (examples provided on the page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given include: “We must not confuse dissent with disloyalty...”, “To be persuasive we must be believable...”, “The speed of communications is wondrous to behold...”, “Difficulty is the excuse history never accepts.” Use these to illustrate the award's values in promotional materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short video promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Record a 30-second or less video about what winning a Murrow Award means to you. Tag @RTDNA (On Instagram: @rtdna.news) and use #Murrow when sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep video under 30 seconds, include the RTDNA tag/handle and hashtag, and post to social platforms as part of the recommended promotion tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards presented to organizations (not individuals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Murrow Awards are presented to news organizations, not individuals (except in the Student categories). Individuals may add Murrow Award language to biographies and social profiles. RTDNA does not verify individual employment work on Murrow-winning pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming association with a winning entry, organizations should be primary recipients; individuals can note association but RTDNA will not verify personal employment/credit on the entry. Keep organizational attribution consistent with award rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plaque and trophy distribution rules
rubrics_metrics.description: One Regional plaque per award is presented to the winning station with details as submitted on the award entry form. Personalized duplicates may be ordered for individuals. One National trophy per award is presented to the winning station, with details as submitted on the award entry form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official physical awards are issued to the station per submitted entry details; individuals seeking personalized items must order duplicates separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement and judging process
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional winners are automatically considered for a National award. Regional winners automatically advance to national judging, which also includes national network entries. Network competitors are judged at the national level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that regional success moves entries into national consideration automatically; national competition includes network entries and has separate judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitive winners listing
rubrics_metrics.description: RTDNA.org winner pages should be considered the definitive list of Murrow Award winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the RTDNA website for authoritative verification of winners rather than third-party claims or local announcements that conflict with the official list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to Murrow Awards Brand Book
rubrics_metrics.description: Murrow Awards Brand Book (referenced on the page) governs detailed brand and promotional usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For full brand standards, logo specifications, and more detailed guidance beyond this page, consult the Murrow Awards Brand Book linked from the RTDNA site.
